# Running method: an adaptive training-plan generator (5K to 100K, road)

A method that builds and adapts running training plans for each runner. It takes into account their level, goal, available time, background and plan length (from a few weeks to several years). This repository holds the written method and, step by step, the software that implements it.

**Status: specification v5.1, not yet implemented.** No plan has been generated by software yet. Nothing here has been tested on runners. It is not medical advice.

## How the method works

- **A competence tree plus rules.** A runner's profile places them in the tree; rules in 7 priority tiers (safety first) build the plan.
- **Generate → validate → repair → fail closed.** A separate validator checks every plan. A plan that fails is never shown; the runner gets ranked options instead.
- **Safety before ambition.** A cap on how much any single run can exceed the recent longest run. Missed sessions are never caught up. An empty answer never unlocks more training.
- **Effort before pace.** Paces come only from measured results. Self-reported data get stricter limits until training logs confirm them (v5.1).
- **Training schools as presets.** Coaching approaches are parameters, not hard-coded truth.
- **Honest evidence grades.** Every rule says whether it rests on evidence, convention or a design default. 206 of 290 rules are design defaults.

## Release profiles

- **MVP:** 5K, 10K and half marathon, default preset.
- **R2:** marathon.
- **R3:** ultra (50K, 100K).

A public release also needs B-1 (PAR-Q+ licence), B-2 (regulatory reading) and B-3 (clinical sign-off). See `spec/00-overview.md`.

## Origin

The method was designed by an LLM council: several AI advisors, neutral expert panels, design rooms, a fact desk and an internal audit, using the [council skill](https://github.com/cleman/council). Sources were web-search summaries only; scientific publishers could not be opened. The grades reflect that.
